stem.text: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a mutation in an allele of the gene that codes for the β-globin polypeptide of haemoglobin.
The diagram shows the sequence of bases in a small section of the template strand of DNA for both the $\text{Hb}^\text{A}$ (normal) and $\text{Hb}^\text{S}$ (sickle cell) β-globin alleles.
Both the polypeptides for $\text{Hb}^\text{A}$ and $\text{Hb}^\text{S}$ are the same length.
How will the mutation in the allele result in the production of an altered version of the β-globin polypeptide?

A.text: A tRNA molecule with the anticodon GUG will form hydrogen bonds with the altered codon on mRNA.

B.text: All the amino acids coded for after the mutation will differ from those in the $\text{Hb}^\text{A}$ protein.

C.text: mRNA transcribed from the $\text{Hb}^\text{S}$ allele will contain the codon CAC instead of the codon CTC.

D.text: The ribosome will be unable to continue translation of the $\text{Hb}^\text{S}$ mRNA after the altered codon.
